description: Panic at src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs:1294 (index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0; out.input_demands[index].join_assign). Reached by the distiller once fz-sc8.137 is in; also panics without it. Cause (verified by instrumentation): ActivationKey::from_inputs (identity.rs:127, via jobs/callable_target.rs derive :66 / world.activation_key) receives an input of type none from the callable surface's inputs (a callback invoked on a map value typed none). types.arrow([none], r) is the top function type and displays as fun, so pure_arrow() is None (types/mod.rs:1371), arrow_arity/input_len is 0, and input_demands is empty while the clause has params. Not the self-nested-closure fold. Minimal program (5 lines): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/census/panic_min.fz; elixir prints %{1 => ""}. Note: with fz-sc8.139's change this program stops panicking and instead reports spec/violation on Enum.join/2 for ({any, any}, binary), which elixir accepts; the none-input key stays reachable. Fix question: a key with a none input is an activation that cannot be called; arity must come from the function, not from the arrow's printed shape.
title: Runtime demand indexes an activation that has no inputs
